name: חיבור שברים רציונליים – מכנים ריבועיים עם גורם משותף (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction:

\[ {{CT:0}}. \]

(Hint: Try factorising the fractions.)

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Factorise the denominators, take the lowest common denominator (the common factor only once), add the numerators and cancel if possible.
Step 1 — Factorise the denominators
When adding or subtracting algebraic fractions, just using the general rule can create a lot more work if the denominators of the fractions have common factors. In this example, if we factorise the denominators (two numbers with the right product and sum) we obtain:

\[ \frac{{CT:1}}{{CT:2}}+\frac{{CT:3}}{{CT:4}}. \]

Step 2 — The lowest common denominator
It is clear that the factor \({{CT:5}}\) is common in both denominators and so there is no need for our common denominator to contain this factor twice. Therefore, we take the common denominator \({{CT:6}}\):

\[ \frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:6}}+\frac{{CT:8}}{{CT:6}} = {{CT:9}}. \]

Step 3 — Add the numerators
Open the brackets in the numerator and collect the like terms:

\[ {{CT:7}}+\left({{CT:8}}\right)={{CT:10}}+\left({{CT:11}}\right)={{CT:12}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:14}}"]]The numerator is a multiple of \(\left({{CT:5}}\right)\): \({{CT:12}}={{CT:13}}\), so this factor cancels with the denominator.[[else]]The numerator has no factor in common with the denominator, so nothing cancels.[[/if]]

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:9}} \]
